what: Recorded floor for the strict unit-coverage gate. tools/quality/strict/check_coverage_floor.py fails when any counter falls below these numbers - by covered count, so a lost test is caught, and by percentage, so production code added without a test is caught.
whyNotAbsolute: WA X is an Xposed module. Its largest classes resolve obfuscated members of WhatsApp's own classes through Xposed reflection, run inside a hooked Android process, and are exercised by a device rather than by a JVM test.
Unobfuscator.kt alone accounts for 11801 uncovered instructions at 0%. A unit test that covered it would have to reimplement WhatsApp's class layout.
1463 classes have zero unit coverage; 824 of them are in com.wax.module and 391 in com.wax.module.xposed.features, which is the whole hook installation layer.
Requiring 100% of instructions, branches, methods and classes therefore asks for a suite that cannot exist. A gate that cannot pass is not a gate, and this one gates the release path.

Absolute coverage is not achievable for the hooked-process layer by construction. The claim discipline that absolute coverage was standing in for - never claiming support without runtime evidence - is enforced by tools/compatibility/validate_compatibility.py, which fails a `supported` cell that has no resolver evidence and no verifiedAt timestamp.
howToRaise: Raise a floor with: ./gradlew -PstrictCollectAll=true :app:createDebugUnitTestCoverageReport && python3 tools/quality/strict/check_coverage_floor.py --xml app/build/reports/coverage/test/debug/report.xml --suite unit --out /tmp/cov.json --update quality/coverage-baseline.json
Say in the commit message which counters moved and why, so a raised floor reads as a decision rather than as an accident.
